title: Traffic Light Demonstration Layout and Initialization
description: Implement a traffic light demonstration game for kids consisting of a vertical traffic light with three colors (Red, Yellow, Green). The initial state should have all lights turned off.
acceptance_criteria:
- A vertical traffic light layout is displayed with Red at the top, Yellow in the middle, and Green at the bottom.
- Three buttons are provided, one for each corresponding light.
- All lights are off by default on initial load.
comment: Assumption confirmed by user: Vertical layout, all lights initially off.

title: Traffic Light Button Toggles and State Logic
description: Provide interactive buttons for each light (Red, Yellow, Green) that allow users to toggle the state of the individual lights. Only one light can be active at a time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clicking a button for an inactive light turns that light on.
- Clicking a button for a light that is currently on turns it off.
- Turning on any light automatically turns off any other light that is currently active, ensuring a maximum of one light is on at any time.
comment: Assumption confirmed by user: Only one light active at a time.

title: Traffic Light Timer Input Configuration and Controls
description: Provide an input text box to specify the automatic color switching interval in seconds and a toggle control button to start and stop the automatic timer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A numeric text box input allows the user to specify the timer interval in seconds, defaulting to 3 seconds.
- The timer interval input requires a positive number (greater than 0); non-positive or invalid inputs are prevented or ignored.
- A control button labeled "Start Timer" initiates the automatic cycling using the configured interval.
- When the timer is active, the control button toggles to display "Stop Timer" and halts cycling when clicked.
comment: Assumptions established based on Issue #2 clarification: default 3s interval, Start/Stop toggle button. Unit test suite in workspace/Tests/Unit/timer.test.js covers interval configuration, validation, and start/stop controls.

title: Automatic Color Switching Cycle and Manual Interruption Logic
description: Implement the automatic transition cycle through traffic light colors at the specified interval, preserving single active light mutual exclusion and properly handling manual interruption.
acceptance_criteria:
- While the timer is active, the traffic light sequentially transitions colors in the order: Red -> Green -> Yellow -> Red at the configured interval.
- If no light is active when the timer starts, the cycle begins by illuminating Red.
- Only one light is active at any point in the cycle, preserving mutual exclusion.
- Clicking any individual color button (Red, Yellow, Green) or clicking Stop Timer immediately halts the automatic timer.
comment: Assumptions established based on Issue #2 clarification: sequential cycle Red -> Green -> Yellow -> Red, manual click halts auto-cycle. Unit test suite in workspace/Tests/Unit/timer.test.js covers cycle progression, initial light rule, mutual exclusion, and manual button interruption.
